title: Abelian sections, alternating rows and coproduct total for ring-module sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ be its small pro-etale site [sk-def-pe-site], let $R$ be an arbitrary sheaf of rings on this site, let $U$ be a site object, and let $W_\bullet$ be a simplicial object over $U$. Work with $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and abelian groups in any common universe containing the site and coefficient universes. Define the abelian evaluation functor $M\mapsto M(U)$ by forgetting the $R(U)$-module structure. Define the cosimplicial abelian sections of $M$ to have degree $r$ equal to $M(W_r)$, with the actual restriction maps induced by $W$. Define its alternating row complex in nonnegative simplicial degrees by $\delta^r=\sum_{i=0}^{r+1}(-1)^i\partial_i^*$ and extend it by zero to negative integer degrees. For any integer cochain complex $K$ of $R$-module sheaves, apply these rows degreewise, put simplicial degree first by flipping the resulting bicomplex, and take the coproduct total [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Its degree $q$ is $\bigoplus_{r\geq0,\,r+m=q}K^m(W_r)$ and its differential on bidegree $(r,m)$ is $\delta+(-1)^r d_K$. Module-sheaf morphisms and coefficient chain maps act by their section maps on every component. These definitions require no covering, affineness, weak contractibility, boundedness or qcqs hypotheses.
